title: Introduce intake credential orchestrator and privacy-safe sampled affinity heatmap exporter
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding workflows currently accept free-form metadata which makes downstream changelog automation brittle and prevents signing/credentialing of intake payloads. This PR introduces an intake credential orchestrator that issues and validates short-lived, signed onboarding credentials; it also introduces a privacy-aware sampled affinity heatmap exporter that produces small, anonymized artifacts used by changelog generation and release teasers.

What this change does: adds a credential minting & verification layer for model intake, wires a new CLI hook (intakectl export-heatmap) and server-side exporter to produce epoched heatmaps from sampled telemetry, and integrates the artifacts into the changelog-autodraft pipeline so release notes can include small, privacy-safe perf snapshots. The orchestrator supports both local keypairs (dev) and integration with the KMS-backed signer used by Private deployments.

Design notes: the credential contract is intentionally minimal: a scoped nonce, model_id, sanitized sample hash, and a short TTL (1h) to limit replay risk. The heatmap exporter runs sampling hooks that respect the onboard metadata_keeplist and applies differential-privacy noise (configurable epsilon) before emitting compact PNG + JSON metadata that changelog-generator consumes. Exporter outputs go to the existing release-briefs bucket with a new prefix to avoid cross-contamination.

Testing and migration: added unit + integration tests that exercise KMS signer (mocked) and local dev signer, sampling rate governor, and the changelog-autodraft end-to-end flow. Migration: existing intakes without credentials are accepted with a deprecation warning for 30 days; a Linear task will track rollout.

Security & privacy: credentials are signed and short-lived to reduce attack surface. Samples are sanitized and no raw prompts or model outputs are included in export artifacts. Reviewed with security: SUP-321 documented the threat model and allowed config.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on credential boundary checks (src/onboard/credential_orchestrator.py), sample sanitizer (exporters/heatmap_exporter.py), and the new intakectl CLI entry. The changelog integration is small glue (hooks/changelog-sampler.yaml) but important for automation completeness.
